As you enter The Royal Dick is situated to the right (with a ramp at the rear) or there is a ramp directly ahead that leads into the main building

Title: Bamboozled
Description: Artists Sonia Killmann and Constant Vigier invite you to their house-warming party at the French Institute in Scotland. The set up will be cosy, just like in a living room. There will be live piano and electronic music, dance and projections. Get your party hats on!
Warnings:
The visuals might be quite quick and colourful at times. The audience will not be involved in the show and the performers will not be wearing masks (however the audience is advised to do so in line with current guidelines).
Strobe lighting, More information
Venue description: The Institut français d'Ecosse has been a historic Edinburgh Festival Fringe partner since opening in 1946. Our "Vive le Fringe !" programme highlights exceptional live performance from French and European artists and delivers events in conjunction with the International Festival, the Book Festival, and the Art Festival. Featuring fine dining and family-friendly shows, our stunning venue in the heart of the Old Town is an unmissable attraction for Fringe audiences.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The Institut français d’Ecosse and the main performance space (Salle Emilienne Moreau-Evrard) are fully accessible with step-free access available. Because of current health guidelines, we operate with a one-way system throughout the building with entrance via George IV Bridge only and exit through West Parliament Square

Title: Violate (Musically)!
Description: Change takes time and courage. Anger, fear and pain however are the true feelings of a victim of sexual violence. Tabitha Combe plays three roles in this hard-hitting piece of musical theatre. Music performed and composed by Bernard Denis (guitar) and Tabitha Combe with Nicky Corcra (double bass). The performance includes up-to-date statistics. Originally performed in French, a Spanish version is in preparation. The show is suitable only for those over the age of 18 because of its upsetting content however the company hopes to target schools and universities. Based in southern France, Communic'Art organises year-round artistic events.
Warnings: Contains distressing themes, Scenes of sexual violence, Strong language/swearing
Venue description: The venue is on the ground floor of a classic 200-year-old Georgian townhouse looking north across the Forth from Calton Hill.
Venue accessibility: Royal Terrace is flat and approached up a gradient either from the top of Leith Walk/London Road or Abbeyhill. The basement entrance is accessed by stone steps down from street level. The main entrance to the building has access from a single stone step preceeded by a 'run-in' and four stone steps up from the pavement. There is a portable ramp to help wheelchair users enter. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The basement bar is inaccessible to wheelchairs

Title: La Serva Padrona
Description: Since 2020, Coronavirus has threatened to kill opera! Can David save it with his one-man production of La Serva Padrona? Baroque meets funk in this new English version of Pergolesi’s 1733 comic masterpiece. 'Possessed of a fine voice with an enormous range… his energy carries his audience along as if surfing a wave' (FringeReview.co.uk). 'It’s a hoot, a bawdy entertainment, and a display of consummate musicality that brings tears to the eyes' **** (ScotsGay Arts). 'Hughes succeeds sensationally' (Boston Musical Intelligencer, classical-scene.com). ***** (MusicalTalk). **** (Advertiser, Adelaide). **** (FringeGuru.com). **** (The730Review.co.uk).
Venue description: The modern festival's smartest multi-space destination venue. The ultimate powerhouse of live performance, offering a pulsating programme of diverse and inclusive work from every genre possible. Part of our 10-space hub at the very stylish Surgeons Quarter, well-stocked bars and great food has made this the perfect destination for audiences who tend to come and spend the day seeing a wide selection of award winning shows from across the globe.
Venue accessibility: Please contact us directly if you have any questions regarding disability access. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. There is a ramp to the venue entrance. Three of the theatres are on the ground floor and there is a passenger lift to the Grand Theatre

Title: Europe's Most Wanted!
Description: In this diverse and friendly stand-up show, Europe's funniest comedians come together with the most well-travelled acts from the rest of the world! They will recall their most outlandish and embarrassing travel stories and quirky observations of their own cultures, all in one room, with no social (or emotional) distancing. Come down to have a laugh and a drink with prime nomads of the comedy world. Different line-ups each night, experienced MCs and lots of fun and fresh insight are guaranteed.
Artist: Steal The Show Comedy / Free Festival
Venue description: Decked out as an authentic American Diner, The Caf has earned a reputation for being jam-packed with local legends, friendly staff and great music since the early 80s. Located between the Royal Mile and the Cowgate. Food is served from 09:00-22:00 every day with free Fringe shows throughout the day (and night!). Venue rooms are fully air conditioned and kids are allowed on the premises until 22:00.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Steep hill to venue entrance. Ramp available on request for entry to City Cafe main bar area (not able to access Fringe shows - these involve steps to basement)

Title: Double Unhappiness
Description: At a wedding banquet in Hong Kong, guests grapple with absurdist small talk, social awkwardness and an unshakable sense of paralysis in the changeable city. Double Unhappiness is a collection of tragicomic monologues exploring family, self-love, self-hate, office life, gossip life and everything else that makes life in the 2020s special. This is the third international tour of Hong Kong’s award-winning Shax Theatre Group, a youthful and multi-ethnic troupe of undergraduates, postgraduates and academics who banded together to introduce Western theatre to the Asian public.
Warnings: Contains distressing themes, Scenes of violence, Strong language/swearing
Venue description: Welcome to Infirmary Street! We can't wait to welcome you into our beautiful venue. We have four fantastic spaces this year showcasing the very best that the fringe has to offer. Hope to see you there!
Venue accessibility: Our website has a tab dedicated to providing you with the most up to date accessibility information. Please take the first entrance when entering the venue from the Bridges. Here there is a doorbell clearly labelled Greenside Wheelchair access. Please ring the doorbell and a member of staff will arrive to assist you

Title: The Three Seas
Description: Be transported into the supernatural world of The Three Seas. An international, cross-cultural ensemble fusing West Bengali Baul music and Himalayan folk song with contemporary sounds from Sydney and Kolkata. The remarkable members of this band were drawn together by a deep love of music, a mutual respect for their distinct and diverse cultural origins and a shared passion for creating songs that resonate universally. Soaring vocals and majestic melodies from North Indian folk traditions are combined with Bengali beats and the deep groove of the baritone saxophone in an energetic, uplifting musical alchemy that radiates joy.
Venue description: Assembly Checkpoint is Fringe's premier venue for cabaret, music and more. The venue is located inside an old church and exudes warmth and charm. There is a bar inside the upstairs venue and further drinking and refreshments options downstairs.
Venue accessibility: Large flight of 26 stone steps up to the performance venue, which is on the first floor. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Vir Das: Wanted
Description: Vir Das, fresh off an Emmy nomination for his latest Netflix stand-up special, brings his brand new Wanted world tour to Edinburgh – a show about freedom, a journey into foolishness and a perspective that takes you across the world. The New York Times declares 'no artist embodies the globalization of stand-up like Vir Das' and the Boston Globe hails the 'mixture of audacity and humility in Das' comedy.' Catch the global phenomenon, who has four specials on Netflix and can most recently be seen in the Judd Apatow film The Bubble on Netflix.
Venue description: The Pleasance’s famous cobblestone Courtyard has be entertaining festival audiences since 1985 and is considered by many to be the very heart of the Fringe. With comedy, theatre and children’s shows once again surrounding our iconic totem pole, this is the place to celebrate the return of the Fringe. ‘The centre of the cultural universe' (Scotsman).
Venue accessibility: A full accessibility guide can be found at www.pleasance.co.uk. Customers with access requirements are encouraged to contact the venue in advance and to make themselves known to a member of the team upon arrival. Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The Pleasance Courtyard is located uphill when accessing the venue from Cowgate. The outdoor spaces of the venue are a mix of cobblestones and tarmacked surfaces

Title: Eleanor Tiernan: Away With The Fairies
Description: Glorious mistakes. Glaring errors. Gallant tales of mischief and misconduct. A bonkers hour of stand-up, story and song from Fest's idiot savant. 'Funny, fanciful and fearless' (Graham Norton). 'Masterful' (Chortle). 'Amiably acerbic' (Stewart Lee). 'Cliché-free and completely unconventional' (Herald). 'Runs the gamut from stupidity to sharp, humane to topsy-turvy hilarious... brilliantly original, logic-askew epiphanies' (Fest).
Artist: Lisa Richards by arrangement with Avalon
Venue description: An exciting, vibrant, neo-gothic mini-castle housing nine performance spaces and six bars. A must for all Fringe-goers. A massive mini-Fringe under one roof, this iconic venue has spawned the best of the best on the Fringe!
Venue accessibility: For further information about accessibility at Gilded Balloon venues email accessibility@gildedballoon.co.uk. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The building is accessed by nine steps up or an external platform lift. For further information visit www.gildedballoon.co.uk/accessibility

Title: Gearóid Farrelly: Glamour Hammer
Description: Gearóid's back from two years on the couch with his cat. It's back to trousers instead of tracksuit bottoms and coffee and a biscuit instead of four gin and tonics and half a cheese cake. In this show Gearóid takes a look at the litany of things in our lives that just don't quite measure up. Everything from his generic-looking cat to Shania Twain. 'Gearóid Farrelly is bloody hilarious' (Sarah Millican). 'My absolute favourite' (Joanne McNally). 'The best opening act in his price range' (Joan Rivers). 'A force to be reckoned with' (Irish Independent).

Title: Masterclass
Description: Featuring the savagely comedic feminist discourse of Adrienne Truscott with the slippery dramaturgy of Brokentalkers, Masterclass parodies the "great male artist" to within an inch of his life to uncover some difficult truths about privilege and power. The show begins in the form of a cockamamie masterclass performed by fed-up feminist Adrienne Truscott and all-around good guy Feidlim Cannon. It's fun. It's familiar. But there is something more at play. Using the arts world as a metaphor, Masterclass is a literate and hilarious examination of gender and power. Supported by Culture Ireland.
Warnings: Contains distressing themes, Scenes of violence, Strong language/swearing
Venue description: The Pleasance Dome is at the very centre of the now famous Bristo Square, featuring the very best comedy and theatre in five venues all under one roof. With great bars and cafes, come soak up the legendary Pleasance atmosphere throughout the day and stay for the fun late in to the night.
Venue accessibility: All performance spaces are accessible. A full accessibility guide can be found at www.pleasance.co.uk. A full accessibility guide can be found at www.pleasance.co.uk. Customers with access requirements are encouraged to contact the venue in advance and to make themselves known to a member of the team upon arrival to access lifts

Title: Sex Me I'm Irish
Description: Ireland’s own Duffy Connors is taking his solo show to Edinburgh. Through his probably too honest one-liners about his romantic life, you can piece together the clues as to why he has been forced to do an Edinburgh show in search of someone decidedly less picky. Is publicly begging for sex the best way to find a woman? Probably not but the odd man is out of ideas. Duffy’s style is a wonderfully contradictory blend of smugness and self-deprecation leaving his dates and audiences to wonder if he loves himself too much or not enough.
Venue description: Decked out as an authentic American Diner, The Caf has earned a reputation for being jam-packed with local legends, friendly staff and great music since the early 80s. Title: Science Magic XXX
Description: Science! Sex! Stand-up! Triple award-winning Irish comedian and scientist, Donal Vaughan has done stand-up for 10 years. For the last five years, he’s also done an acclaimed sell-out science show for children. Now, for the first time, he’s putting the shows together for a raunchy science comedy show, strictly for adults only. In his new show, Donal will perform amazing science tricks, interspersed with hilarious comedy. Always rude and sometimes very messy, laugh your ass off and learn about science in a unique show that will need to be seen to be believed.
Venue description: Located within the five-star A&O Edinburgh Hostel, Bar 50 is a bar and restaurant offering three rooms of free Fringe shows, drinks and tasty, locally sourced pub grub in laid-back, modern and stylish surroundings, an outdoor beer garden and balcony beer terrace.

Title: Science Magic
Description: The fun, family, science comedy show is back! New tricks this year include popping a balloon with an orange, a twist on the famous table cloth trick, a device that runs electricity through your body and a giant air cannon. Using only things you find around the house, Donal will perform amazing tricks to show how magical science can be. Always exciting and sometimes very messy, learn about science and laugh your pants off while you do. Strongly recommended to book a ticket to secure a seat. The shows will sell out fast.
Venue description: Edinburgh's premier party venue and the a central free Fringe hub with three rooms of free shows running throughout the day and night, all located off of a vibrant and buzzing courtyard in the middle of Cowgate. With a huge drinks selection, a wide bar menu and a courtyard plenty with plenty of space to chill out or party outside. Shows run from 10am to 2am.

Title: That Black Mirror Episode With the Two Lesbians – 2
Description: Ireland's comedy darlings Mark O'Keeffe (Winner Show Me the Funny 2019) & Richy Sheehy (viral sensation as seen on Sky, RTE, BBC) are back with their new best hour! 'These guys are going to be f*cking huge' (David McSavage). 'Great f*cking set' (Tony Hinchcliffe). 'Most original, first-class comedy' (Limerick Fringe).

Title: Brian Gallagher: Another Funny Irishman, Blah Blah, Diddley Diddle Dee
Description: True stories, sharp gags and a big beard – Gallagher returns to Fringe following his sold-out run last time out! From growing up in Ireland, to travelling the world and everything in-between; this show blends unbelievable true stories, killer crowd work, smart jokes and blistering wit. An unmissable show from one of Ireland's favourite stand-up comedians. As seen on RTE TV. 'One to Watch' (Hotpress.com). 'The big stage beckons' (City Limits Comedy Club). 'Promising show!' (ThreeWeeks). 'Charming/Entertaining' (Student). Buy a ticket now... blah blah, diddley diddle dee.
Venue: Scottish Comedy Festival @ The Beehive Inn
Venue description: Situated in the Grassmarket, the heart of historic Old Edinburgh, and serving food and drink all day long, The Beehive Inn comprises a main bar on the ground floor and a comfortable and relaxing restaurant and bar on the first floor. Our two dedicated 50-seat performance spaces, presenting some of the best home-grown comedy at the Festival, are on the first and second floors.

Title: Irish Jokers
Description: A compilation show of the best Irish acts at the Fringe as well as award-winning comedians who are flying over, just to do this show. This is the first stop for busy Irish club comedians who are popping over to the Fringe for a few days. Fast paced and gags aplenty! This show will be guaranteed hilarity every night! Expect adult themes and language.

Title: Ireland's Best Themed Show: Tree Fiddy
Description: Dublin's favourite comedy club is on tour. Each night, a trending theme is picked and top comics battle it out to win a coveted Tree Fiddy medal. If something big happened today, then it's probably the theme of tonight's show. Each night has a new theme and a new line-up of hand-picked top comedians of the Fringe! Check @treefiddycomedy for tonight's theme.
Venue description: An Irish bar with a difference... we're actually Irish! Located just off Edinburgh's famous Grassmarket, Dropkick Murphy's gives you a real experience of what an Irish bar is meant to be. Live music at night, major sports on big screens, and our great craic assured – plus free shows here through the Fringe from midday to 10pm with the bar open until very late afterwards! STRICTLY OVER 18s ONLY
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, No wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Vinegar
Description: Dublin poet Rob McGlade performs a selection of poems from his debut collection, Vinegar. Featuring potential classics like Uncle Oncological, A Raw Na Veen, Je'member, The Seven Deadly Commandments, and of course, Being A Man Is Like Being A Dog With A Split Personality. As The New Yorker has said, they won't be carrying his work in their magazine.
Venue description: A lively and trendy gay-friendly cafe/bar venue. Situated over two floors for eating, drinking and dancing. Now open until 3am. During the Fringe we host a selection of PBH Free Fringe shows in our function room from 12noon-midnight. Over 18s only.

Title: LOL?
Description: Can we still laugh at this? Let's find out. This is 10 years of material, rubbed and polished into pristine comedy and premiering at this year's Fringe.
Venue description: The Counting House has been a free venue for over a decade, and is one of the largest free venues in Edinburgh, with six rooms between this venue and it's linked venues 32 Below and The Pear Tree every day from 10:00 to 03:00. There's a massive outdoor courtyard, four bars, a full restaurant food selection and giant Outdoor screen. What better place could you hang out during the Fringe?

Title: Abandoman aka Rob Broderick: Discography
Description: Using his innate ability to craft songs on the spot, Rob creates a full discography for a fictional artist created by you, the audience. Using a sample pad necklace to trigger high-production beats, Rob creates the kind of exhilarating live experience that has won him a string of awards, and the highest of international critical acclaim. He continues to sell out his Fringe runs in Edinburgh and Australia each year, wowing audiences wherever he plays. 'Clever, quick-witted and audacious' **** (Scotsman). 'Raucous, expansive and relentless hilarious' **** (Times). 'Truly innovative' (Guardian).
Warnings: Audience participation, Strobe lighting, Strong language/swearing
Venue description: Come and graze in George Square! Food, drink, two fantastic venues and, of course, an upside-down purple cow. If you're looking for Udderbelly, the Wee Coo and a place to soak up the Fringe atmosphere, this is the place to be.

Title: The Circus Sonas Family Show
Description: Circus Sonas are Northern Irish father and son Martin and Logy. Top-class circus entertainment and the two best beards in the business. There will be clapping, cheering and lots and lots of laughing. This is a family-friendly show that is suitable for all ages and abilities. 'If you’re looking for a show for the whole family that mum and dad will also enjoy, go see this one. Martin and Logy are a hoot, and they can even juggle.' (GlamAdelaide.com.au).

Title: Des Bishop: Mia Mamma
Description: My mother died in March 2019 and of course it was sad and grief can be tough sometimes, but I saw a lot of funny in that too. Since death comes to us all and grief is something most of us will experience, I thought there must be plenty of people who would like that funny to be shared. She was a complicated person and this isn't just about death. It's about motherhood, sacrifice, anxiety, generational legacy of trauma, regret and, of course, loss, grief and the chaos that surrounds it.
Artist: Lisa Richards by arrangement with Off The Kerb
Venue description: Assembly Gordon Aikman Theatre (formerly George Square Theatre) , The Box and The Blue Room are perfectly located next to Assembly George Square Gardens and Studios for pre or post-show refreshments. The Theatre is a purpose-built venue seating up to 500, The Box is an intimate 74-seat studio and The Blue Room is a unique 130-seater studio all hosting an array of world-class shows.

Title: Stephen Mullan: Ouch!
Description: Stephen Mullan arrives at the Edinburgh Fringe bringing his special brand of goofy energetic comedy to the festival for the first time. Fresh from his trip to Love Island Australia, Stephen returned to Ireland to find himself on a new adventure of searching for love himself. This brand-new hour is a celebration of all the things that make us go Ouch! From life as a single dad, to the pain of returning to school as an adult, Ireland's favourite cheeky son is guaranteed to make you howl with this silly and ridiculous spectacle.
Venue description: Located opposite the Assembly George Square Gardens entrance and next to Assembly George Square Theatre. The five Studios have some of the best audience facilities on the Fringe, with comfortable modern seating. The indoor Studios Bar has plenty of sofas and freshly prepared hot and cold meals. The Flick at Underground and the new immersive venue The Cubicle at Buccleuch Place are also found here.

Title: Neil Delamere: Liminal
Description: Fresh from a sell-out tour, star of BBC's The Blame Game, Fighting Talk and The News Quiz, Neil Delamere returns to Edinburgh with a brand-new show. Whether it's between countries or systems, the place in the middle often looks the most interesting. 'You'll be hard pressed to find a more gifted comic at the Fringe' ***** (Scotsman).

Title: Foil Arms and Hog – Hogwash
Description: Ireland’s top sketch comedy group. With over 500 million online views the internet sensations return to McEwan Hall to premiere their new show, Hogwash. A mix of sketch comedy, audience participation and improvisation. Best reviewed show at the Edinburgh Fringe 2018 and 2019. Sold out 2009-2019. 'Quite simply, a sensation' (Edinburgh Festivals Magazine). 'Very funny show' (Rowan Atkinson). 'Hilarious lads' (Kevin Bridges). 'An effervescent hour of fast-paced gags, fizzing with energy, invention and great lines' (Chortle.co.uk). **** (Times). ***** (Irish Examiner). ***** (BroadwayBaby.com). ***** (Metro). ***** (EdFestMag.com).
Venue description: Situated at the heart of the festival, Bristo Square is where you can find a variety of venues, including the magnificent McEwan Hall, presenting theatre, musicals, comedy, cabaret and family shows early 'til late.

Title: Andrew Maxwell: Krakatoa
Description: Double Edinburgh Comedy Award nominee. 'Furiously funny' (Times). 'One of the funniest men in Britain' (Telegraph). 'If you can only see one stand-up act, see Maxwell' (Mirror). He's the winner of the Time Out Award for Best Live Comic, Chortle's Best Live Comedian and Channel 4's King Of Comedy. As seen on Live at the Apollo, I'm a Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here, Have I Got News For You, QI, Mock the Week and the winner of Celebrity Mastermind. Andrew is also the voice of MTV's Ex On The Beach.

Title: Ruth Hunter and the Ruth-hunter
Description: There is something living in Ruth's hallway cupboard. Come and see if it kills her good and dead! Ruth is an Irish comedian living in Glasgow who has supported the likes of Fern Brady, Alison Spittle and Kiri Pritchard-McLean. She now presents an hour of spoooky comedy. Don't be afraid; ghosts aren't real. 'Subversive So You Think You're Funny finalist Ruth Hunter presents an excellent debut hour' **** (Skinny). 'I was truly impressed with Ruth Hunter' (Scotsman). 'Warm, funny and relatable' (EdinburghGuide.com).
Warnings: Scenes of a sexual nature, Strong language/swearing
Venue description: The Banshee Labyrinth is a teeming pub that is said to be Scotland's most haunted pub. Three performance spaces, three bars, one open from 12.30-05:00. Over 18s only. www.thebansheelabyrinth.com
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site

Title: Aidan Greene: I Know What You Did Last Stammer
Description: Award-winning Irish comedian Aidan Greene has stammered since he was four years old. He's managed to make that funny. But what if he had never stammered at all? Don't worry, it'll still be funny. Come see how having a disability can shape a life by looking at a life without it. 'A show which is as heartfelt as hilarious' **** (TheWeeReview.com). 'Aidan Greene clearly has a talent for comedy, and harnessing his gift has given him an authentic edge at this Edinburgh Festival Fringe' **** (Deadline.com).
Venue description: Situated at the heart of the festival, Bristo Square is where you can find a variety of venues, including the magnificent McEwan Hall, presenting theatre, musicals, comedy, cabaret and family shows early 'til late.

Title: When Judas Met John – Songs of Dylan and Lennon
Description: Influenced by the meeting of Bob Dylan and The Beatles, Irish duo Brothers Broke compare, adapt and perform a unique interpretation of songs by both artists. This casual and engaging 45-minute show compares the like-minded and socially conscious lyrics of Dylan and The Beatles, in particular, Lennon. The duo modify and present the songs in a blues/folk style with tight sibling harmonies, around a story of the influence, jealousy, parody and respect that each artist had for the other.
Venue description: Next door to theSpace @ Surgeons Hall, theSpaceTriplex makes up part of our fabulously smart destination hub of 10 performance spaces located right at the heart of the modern Fringe and offers an unmissable platform of diverse live performance. Music, dance, theatre, physical theatre, a capella, opera, comedy and cabaret. A vibrant programme of performance, all under one roof in the most spectacular space in town.

Title: Sitting on a Cornflake – Songs of Lennon and McCartney
Description: Influenced by the songwriting of Lennon and McCartney, Irish duo Brothers Broke compare, adapt and perform a unique interpretation of songs by both artists from their Beatles and solo careers. This alluring acoustic 45-minute show compares the individual styles and personalities that contributed to a unique partnership that saw both composers constantly driven to better themselves. Brothers Broke modify and present the songs in an acoustic blues and folk style, exploring influence, inspiration and the competitiveness of this collaborative, yet often independent, songwriting partnership.

Title: Anna Clifford: I SEE DEAD(LY) PEOPLE
Description: Facing an existential crisis Anna powered off her phone and dived head first into an Ayahuasca retreat in the Irish wilderness. Days later she returned a changed woman, but that's not all that changed. The world had entered a global pandemic, Anna's boyfriend had ghosted her and her Mother announced she kinda, might die! In a hilarious show about positivity versus the world, Anna will have you in stitches with real stories that are unbelievable! Irish comedian Anna is a Funny Women finalist and has worked for BBC, RTE and the Vodafone Comedy Festival.

Title: Prince of Denmark
Description: This prelude to Shakespeare's most famous tragedy imagines Hamlet as a restless teenager frustrated by the limits of his role and furious at his father's warmongering ways. It provides a fascinating backstory to Hamlet and a sophisticated insight into the psyche of its hero, making it ideal for all ages. A top-notch 50 minutes... it's superb and breathtakingly eloquent, writing at its best.
Venue description: Right in the middle of it all in the best location and part of our Royal Mile hub (10 theatres) we present two very special spaces, offering an array of new and established work – from theatre to musicals, dance, comedy and music, a real feast for all. The buzzing courtyard bar adjacent to the venue offers audiences pre and post-show drinks and an unrivalled fringe experience.

Title: After
Description: In 2017, I was raped. For years after, I avoided my feelings on it. I thought I was alone in the whirlwind of anger, confusion and numbness. When I began seeing people online talk about their stories and heard how similar they were to my own, I realised the power of sharing my story with others. This play features true stories from survivors of sexual assault and the detrimental effects that it can have After.
Venue description: The modern festival's smartest multi-space destination venue. The ultimate powerhouse of live performance, offering a pulsating programme of diverse and inclusive work from every genre possible. Part of our 10-space hub at the very stylish Surgeons Quarter, well-stocked bars and great food has made this the perfect destination for audiences who tend to come and spend the day seeing a wide selection of award winning shows from across the globe.

Title: La Merda
Description: **** (Guardian, Times). Winner of six major theatre awards at the Fringe including Scotsman Fringe First and The Stage Best Actress Award. La Merda's poetic and shocking stream of consciousness on the human condition has thrilled sell-out audiences around the world, from Europe to Brazil and Australia to North America. To celebrate its 10th anniversary, Cristian Ceresoli’s acclaimed original production returns for 12 special shows in the same intimate space where this international theatre phenomenon began, with Silvia Gallerano reprising her award-winning unmissable performance. 'One of the most wonderful full on performances ever seen in Edinburgh' **** (Scotsman).
Artist: Frida Kahlo Productions and Richard Jordan Productions with Summerhall
Venue description: Summerhall presents engaging, challenging and exhilarating theatre, music, dance and visual arts for people of all ages in the atmospheric buildings of Edinburgh’s former Royal (Dick) Veterinary College. There’s delicious food and drink in our own Royal Dick bar and Summerhall Café, plus al fresco bars and street food in the buzzing festival courtyard. The full programme of performance and exhibitions is at www.summerhall.co.uk
Venue accessibility:
We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. 

If coming into Summerhall using the main entrance please be aware that there are nine steps up to reception and the steps do not have a handrail.

Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café and our accessible venues. 

Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, there is parking using either pay and display machines or single yellow line spaces on Summerhall Square beside our step free access. Please be aware that this street is a dead end, and quite short and therefore parking there can be quite competitive.

We have lift access to some of the First Floor spaces and the Basement spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the Box Office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please contact us by phone on 0131 560 1581 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

http://www.summerhall.co.uk/about/accessibility
. Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. Title: Classical Guitar and Bel Canto
Description: After the debut in 2019 of Duo Corde InCanto, the versatile soprano Silvia Mirarchi and refined guitarist Luca Villani return with a new recital spanning five centuries of music for voice and guitar. Renaissance Songs by John Dowland, popular Lascia ch’io pianga by Haendel, the sparkling Di tanti palpiti by Giuliani-Rossini, the poignant Dolente Immagine di fille mia by Bellini and the intriguing Voi che sapete by Mozart. In the second part firing Canciones españolas by Manuel de Falla, When the morning of life by Castelnuovo-Tedesco and El cantar de los Cantares by Leo Brouwer.
Artist: Corde InCanto (Silvia Mirarchi and Luca Villani)
Venue description: Festival Fringe productions in The Little Theatre 'beyond the treasure house of salamis, cheeses, balsamic vinegars and olive oils' (Sunday Times). 'If anything makes a London-based gourmet jealous of the Scots, it is Valvona & Crolla' (Financial Times).

Title: Guitar Dances
Description: After a two-year break, Luca Villani returns to play for local and international guitar enthusiasts new pieces and beloved works, like the Albèniz Asturias and the Aguado Rondò. Luca will play different Valses such as Tàrrega Grand Vals, Tchaikovsky Sentimental Valse, Miguel Llobet's dreamlike Scherzo-Vals, the popular Vals op.8 n.4 by Barrios, with its Latin-American feeling, the joyful Ponce Mexican Vals and the Villa-Lobos Valsa-Choro, rich in Brazilian-saudade. The well-known Fandango by Joaquin Rodrigo, the spirited Nikita Koshkin's Usher Vals and Malambo by Cherubito, fiere dance of Argentinian gauchos, sparkling finale to this truly enjoyable guitar recital. http://www.patrickmaillouxluthier.com

Title: Let's Try Gay
Description: Two friends, Jack and Phil, meet in a hotel to shoot a gay adult movie between two straight guys: an “art project” to send to an independent movie festival, but they now feel uncomfortable. Their attempts to even just kiss or hug are clumsy and awkward. As time goes on, they prolong their problems. Jack is struggling with his life as an artist while Phil reveals his doubts about his sexual identity. Freely inspired by the independent movie Humpday, this unlikely comedy turns from a goofy, relaxed, funny situation into a deeper analysis of human nature.
Warnings: Nudity, Scenes of a sexual nature, Strong language/swearing

Wonderfully located in our 10-space hub adjacent to theSpaceTriplex and theSpace @ Surgeons Hall. A programme of music, a capella, theatre and comedy and a stylish prosecco bar and theatre tent in the adjacent tranquil garden. A must for all well-heeled Fringe goers.

Title: Space Hippo
Description: Earth is dying. We can't do anything to stop it. Our only hope is to launch a hippo into space. Along the way she will encounter new worlds, strange alien creatures and end up at the centre of an intergalactic war. Hilarious, weird and epic science fiction from Japan, experienced through award-winning cinematic shadow puppetry. The performers project over two hundred handmade puppets onto a large screen to create a live analogue motion picture before your very eyes. 'More epic than most billion dollar blockbusters' (OrlandoWeekly.com). 'Surprisingly touching and beautifully executed' ***** (CBC).
Venue description: Assembly Gordon Aikman Theatre (formerly George Square Theatre) , The Box and The Blue Room are perfectly located next to Assembly George Square Gardens and Studios for pre or post-show refreshments. The Theatre is a purpose-built venue seating up to 500, The Box is an intimate 74-seat studio and The Blue Room is a unique 130-seater studio all hosting an array of world-class shows.

Title: Six Stories
Description: Taking inspiration from the Korean shamanic rituals known as Gut, WeMu reimagines the traditional in a concert combining Western and Korean instruments, creating modern music based on ancient customs. Gut is a ritual that has been designated as part of Korea’s National Intangible Cultural Heritage and is safeguarded by dedicated preservation societies. In this concert, WeMu breaks down the shamanic rituals into new forms, transforming the welcome and repatriation of deities into a welcome to audiences. Part of the Korean Showcase 2022.

Title: The Names I Have Known You By
Description: A chance meeting changes Annika’s life forever. Has she met the man of her dreams, or is her dream of domestic bliss simply out of reach? Does Annika’s name change to protect the innocent? Or to protect the guilty? Set in the late 90s, a young woman is searching for the perfect relationship and the perfect family but soon realises that domestic bliss is far from her reach. Based on true stories from real women, this a physically engaging piece which seeks to find the extraordinary in the ordinary.
Warnings: Scenes of a sexual nature, Scenes of violence, Strong language/swearing

Title: Paul Williams: In the Moonlight
Description: Join New Zealand’s fastest comedian (5km and 10km) for an enchanting afternoon In the Moonlight. The show includes music, romance and even photos. He’s been on TV, starring in the critically reviewed Taskmaster New Zealand. Good for all ages but if you’re really old, please only come if you promise to stay calm. 'How much of Paul Williams’ endearing clumsiness is planned, and how much is accidental, is difficult to ascertain' (Chortle.co.uk). 'Insanely talented' (Rose Matafeo). **** (Skinny). **** (List).

Title: SNORT
Description: New Zealand’s favourite improv show and the sell-out hit of the 2019 Fringe returns! Cheeky, topical and relentlessly silly, Snort sees a rotating cast of New Zealand’s best comedians (including Rose Matafeo, Laura Daniel, Joseph Moore, Eli Matthewson, Nic Sampson, James Roque, Brynley Stent, Paul Williams, Rhiannon McCall, Freya Finch, Alice Canton and more) build an intricate hour of far-fetched, high-stakes comedy, entirely made-up on the spot, featuring a brand new guest every night. Past guests have included: David O’Doherty, Nish Kumar, Olga Koch and more. ***** (Edinburgh Festivals Magazine). 'An absolute joy to watch' **** (BroadwayWorld.com).
Venue description: The Pleasance’s famous cobblestone Courtyard has be entertaining festival audiences since 1985 and is considered by many to be the very heart of the Fringe. Title: God Damn Fancy Man
Description: Joyful, daring and undeniably sharp, God Damn Fancy Man is the hotly anticipated new show from critically acclaimed, internationally award-winning comedian James Nokise. Covering a thrilling whirlwind of topics with skilful ease and exhilarating energy, Nokise's brand of joyously cathartic stand-up will twist its way into your psyche and leave you delighted. 'Packed full of paternal wisdom and wit' **** (Fest). 'Nokise is a joy to have on stage' ***** (Scotsman).

Description: One time, Alice got kicked out of an airport because her passport was covered in glow stick – and that's just the start. In her much-anticipated debut hour, the award-winning, sell-out New Zealand comedian rips the lid off the reality of life with ADHD. Best Newcomer nominee (NZ Comedy Festival, 2017). Description: A favourite on the New Zealand comedy scene for the last 10 years, Kiwi-Filipino James Roque makes his debut at the Edinburgh Fringe. His entire life, James' family have referred to him by his traditional baby nickname – Badong. Now that Badong has turned 30, he's asking – is it finally time to retire the name? This is a show about embracing adulthood and learning to love your inner grown up, as seen through the eyes of a Filipino migrant who grew up in New Zealand.

Title: Eglantyne
Description: Vibrant, inspiring play about Eglantyne Jebb; visionary, passionate, humanitarian, human rights activist and founder of Save the Children. 'Outstanding performance, a great show' (TheReviewsHub.com). 'Written with wit and buoyancy' (Theatreview.org.nz). 'Light champagne brilliance of presentation, enlightening and moving' (FringeReview.co.uk). In 1919, challenging the British government's lack of response to the devastating famine in post-war Europe, Eglantyne and her sister Dorothy founded Save the Children. From idyllic Shropshire, Eglantyne went onto Oxford University, Cambridge social work, Bloomsbury parties, heartbreaks, suffrage rallies, spiritualism, the Balkans, an arrest in Trafalgar Square and pioneering children's rights. Written and performed by Anne Chamberlain. www.eglantynetheshow.com

Title: HarleQueen
Description: New Zealand comedian Abby Howells weaves together stories of female comedians from history with her own tales of triumph, foolishness and heartbreak. In this award-winning show you will laugh, you will cry, you will not be impressed by Abby's ventriloquists skills, but she will do it anyway. ****1/2 (WeekendNotes.co.uk). Adelaide winner of Festival Director's Pick. New Zealand Comedy Festival winner of Best Comedy, Week Four 2020. Adelaide Fringe Festival winner of Emerging Artist 2020. Adelaide Fringe Festival winner of Best Comedy 2019.

Description: Award-winning Eli Matthewson is taking you back through some huge life revelations that took place in some seriously shitty cars, from when he came out to his dad, to 10 years later when his dad came out to him. Winner of Best Show, NZ International Comedy Festival, 2021. Winner of Director's Award, NZ International Comedy Festival, 2019. 30 Best Jokes of the Edinburgh Fringe, The Telegraph, 2019. Title: Intruder / Intruz
Description: Shortlisted for Adrian Pagan Playwriting Award and BBC Writersroom. Following his dream, Remi moves to Scotland to become an actor. But an ugly and vicious attack almost ruins his life. Dwujezyczny (ang-pol) monodram to wzruszajaca i humorystyczna opowiesc o byciu w zlym miejscu o zlej porze i pokazujacy jak moment moze zmienic cale zycie. Rachuba's writing is heart-wrenching, unique and brutal. With elements of black humour and clever twists, the play keeps the audience transfixed to witness a moving portrayal of acceptance and, ultimately, forgiveness. Performances in English i po polsku.

Her beloved had to leave after the last catastrophe, but he promised to return. Awaiting him, Katie sings and speaks to us through the deafening flow of world events. Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café and our accessible venues. 

Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, there is parking using either pay and display machines or single yellow line spaces on Summerhall Square beside our step free access. Please be aware that this street is a dead end, and quite short and therefore parking there can be quite competitive.

We have lift access to some of the First Floor spaces and the Basement spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the Box Office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please contact us by phone on 0131 560 1581 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

Title: Dedication
Description: 'The past isn’t dead, it’s not even past' (William Faulkner). New York pianist Roger Peltzman’s one–person show, Dedication, recounts his family’s tragic history fleeing the Nazis in war–torn Europe using drama, powerful images and musical performances of everything from blues to Chopin.  Drawn into the story of people he never knew, Peltzman develops a 'relationship' with his uncle, Norbert Stern, a brilliant pianist who was murdered in Auschwitz at age 21.  Learning that Holocaust trauma can be inherited, Peltzman is able to come to terms with himself and a past that becomes present.
Warnings:
Show is about overcoming second generation Holocaust trauma.  Near the end of the play there are descriptions of life and death in Auschwitz.

New York City comedian Katharyn Henson (**** (Skinny) for Ew Girl, You Nasty) presents some of the finest funny female voices at the Fringe. Katharyn, described as a 'hair-raising stand-up' by The Scotsman, has met a lot of funny women while touring her comedy all over the world and she delights in being able to showcase a filthy, funny frenzy of funny female voices in a daily changing line-up of filthy fun.

Title: Ben Miller's Stand-Up Science
Description: A show that's equal measures hilarious, educational and deeply personal. Scientist turned stand-up comedian Ben Miller takes you on a journey that explores everything from milk to the thermodynamics of refrigerators with a wit and humour that makes these topics both approachable and delightful. And you probably like that sort of thing, nerd. Ben Miller is an NYC-based comedian who's currently ranked as the top roast battler in NYC. He has a degree in Materials Science and Engineering, worked on a science bus, 3D printed cookies and has diffused a few bar fights while on stage.

Title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Friends?
Description: When a struggling actor can’t pay rent, she signs herself and her roommate (she won’t mind) up for a fun robot friend in order to receive a big paycheck. Her engineer roommate is less enthused by the prospect of an AI trial placement invading their privacy in order to 'increase EI quotient'. In this innovative media experience, the audience can both explore the virtual world and interact with the characters as Actor and Engineer work with the AI to question what it means to be human: the good, the bad and the electric.
Venue description: Greenside @ Nicolson Square is set in the heart of town, seconds from the Festival Theatre, the flashing lights of Bristo Square and the hustle and bustle of the Royal Mile. We’re bringing our desire for creating great spaces and passion for service to the heart of the festival.

Title: The Marriage of Figaro
Description: Scotland’s professional touring opera company returns with Mozart’s sublime comedy. The big day has arrived for Figaro and Susanna, but a catalogue of twists and turns threatens to spoil it all! Oliver Platt directs a new English version of the opera, with design by Alisa Kalyanova and performed with chamber orchestra, conducted by Alistair Digges. A stellar cast includes Scottish favourite Catriona Clark and former Scottish Opera Emerging Artists Andrew McTaggart, Charlie Drummond and Arthur Bruce. The opera is packed full of wonderful arias, duets and ensembles, all brought to life in this exciting production.
Venue description: The historic Parish Church of St Cuthbert's sits at the very heart of Edinburgh, on Lothian Road near the junction with Princes Street (opposite the Caledonian Hotel), adjacent to public transport and Castle Terrace car park. It has two superb performance spaces and fine acoustics.

Title: William Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet
Description: The children of Cargilfield School present an abridged version of Shakespeare's classic love story, performed in the round in Shakespeare's original language. A modern day sound track, together with mime and dance, make this a memorable experience for both cast and audience. Performed in the intimate setting of the Young Room within the beautiful Stockbridge Parish Church.
Venue description: Situated in the heart of vibrant Stockbridge, ten minutes walk from city centre. Stockbridge Church is an attractive Grade-B Georgian listed building. A magnificent space which has a flexible stage, a balcony with a splendid church organ and separate halls.

Title: Bob Doolally Live and Half-Cut in Qatar
Description:
He’s the man who put the foot into football. Regardless of whether Scotland are there or not, the legendary ex-manager-cum-pundit will be in Doha this year. Meanwhile, he’s back at the Fringe with some more outrageous drink-fuelled predictions for the World Cup, left-field comments and downright filth. Brimful of new material for 2022, plus the ever-popular question and answer session to close the show.
Star of BBC’s BAFTA-nominated Live Floor Show. 'Almost better than football' (Independent). 'All the skill and precision of a Beckham free kick' (Stage).
Artist: Bob Doolally / The Stand Comedy Club
Venue description: The Stand's New Town Theatre is heralding in a new Fringe age of outstanding Comedy, Spoken Word, Theatre, Music and Interactive Game Play in the New Town area! Situated in the beautiful Freemasons' Hall, built in 1913 on George Street, between Assembly Rooms and Charlotte Square, the New Town Theatre is a must visit destination. A beautiful Fringe venue with well-equipped and comfortable theatre spaces.

Title: Ali Affleck Celebrates Nina Simone – Little Girl Blue
Description: A carefully considered celebration of the trailblazing musician Nina Simone. Award-winning Ali and her all-star band (Paul Harrison, Stu Brown, Colin Steele, Roy Percy) span the master musician's career and perform classic works that will stir emotions. An evocative, intimate and passionate journey – some of the most powerful songs written by a true icon! Early booking advised for this exciting Fringe Premiere! ‘Stunningly expressive’ ***** (San Diego Union-Tribune). 'Musical Storyteller' (Scotsman). 'Gorgeous voice... superb precision in using her instrument' (LA Times).

Title: Piano Recital
Description: '…A master….tremendous virtuosity…..seductive….' (EdinburghGuide.com). Alasdair is back with a programme showing how Beethoven and Schubert foreshadowed the Romantic period with works having an increasing dramatic and emotional intensity. The powerful opening of Beethoven's op.111 establishes the drama to follow. The sublime slow movement is in complete contrast. With Schubert we have lyricism and drama, while with Chopin, the heart is fully on the sleeve.

In a fraction of a second go from belly laughing to intense confusion and lose yourself in mystery. Be transfixed, shocked and properly entertained, once again, on a night out where stranger things will happen right before your eyes. Complete sell-out, Edinburgh Fringe 2021. Best Magic, Adelaide Fringe 2018. Scottish Comedy Awards 2018 winner and 2019 nominee. 'Master Illusionist' ***** (Advertiser, Adelaide). 'Astonishing' ***** (Edinburgh Evening News). 'Epic stunts. Classic showstoppers from Phantom of the Opera, Mary Poppins, Chicago, Les Miserables, Oliver… A belter of a one-woman show starring one of Scotland’s top singers with her incredible three-octave range. Title: Charles Maclean Whisky Masterclass
Description: Charles Maclean has been researching and writing books and articles about whisky since 1981. He has published 10 books to date including the standard work on whisky brands, Scotch Whisky and the leading book on the subject, Malt Whisky, both of which were shortlisted for Glenfiddich Awards. He shares his enthusiasm and knowledge by giving talks and tastings around the world. This is a unique opportunity to learn from a whisky legend and to taste a selection of whiskies from across Scotland.

Playing folk music firmly placed in the modern world, Barry's roots are traditional with a fiddle-playing and songwriting background. As one of the world-famous Cullivoe Fiddlers, Barry plays a regional style of Shetland music and a captain of tall ships having sailed the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans. RnR Magazine described his previous album A Bright Ray of Sunshine (2018) as 'Magnificent' in a five-star review.

All box office income will go straight to The Brain Tumour Charity, and Underbelly will match this amount as a donation to the charity, doubling the amount that we can raise on the night. Description:
Scotland’s international comedy star is doing a run of shows to work up some new material for his next tour. So come expecting nerves, notes onstage and a lot of laughs… but don’t come expecting a slick, finished comedy show. This is strictly a work in progress. 
(We should probably also mention that Daniel was the biggest ticket-selling comedian in the world for most of 2021, has sold out six New York solo Off-Broadway seasons, appeared on US TV’s Conan 10 times, broken box office records in Edinburgh and toured in 53 countries).

Title: Dreams of the Small Gods
Description: Dreams of the Small Gods tells the story of the awakening of Wild Woman. Naked, unaware and unselfconscious, she explores her surroundings, more animal than human. Her growing consciousness attracts the attention of a creature from the spirit world, a primal deity who sparks her curiosity and compels her to transform. She changes her physicality, drawing power from the merging of animal, human and spirit self. Inspired by the timeless wisdom of faerie tales, mythology and ancient ritual, Dreams of the Small Gods is a blend of aerial circus, masked ritual and performance art. MadeInScotlandShowcase.com
Artist: Zinnia Oberski presented by Scissor Kick
Venue description: Summerhall presents engaging, challenging and exhilarating theatre, music, dance and visual arts for people of all ages in the atmospheric buildings of Edinburgh’s former Royal (Dick) Veterinary College. There’s delicious food and drink in our own Royal Dick bar and Summerhall Café, plus al fresco bars and street food in the buzzing festival courtyard. The full programme of performance and exhibitions is at www.summerhall.co.uk
Venue accessibility:
We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. 

If coming into Summerhall using the main entrance please be aware that there are nine steps up to reception and the steps do not have a handrail.

Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café and our accessible venues. 

Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, there is parking using either pay and display machines or single yellow line spaces on Summerhall Square beside our step free access. Please be aware that this street is a dead end, and quite short and therefore parking there can be quite competitive.

We have lift access to some of the First Floor spaces and the Basement spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the Box Office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please contact us by phone on 0131 560 1581 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

Description: In Cherub Spring: A Political Satire, turmoil unfolds at a nursery school when the children get tired of Claire choosing all the games they play on the playground and a rebellion breaks out. But Claire doesn’t give up without a fight and political conflict (rife with fear-mongering, back-room dealings and shameless campaigning) unfolds amongst the five-year-olds. An essential show not to be missed by any lover of the guitar or instrumental music, this is a rare opportunity to see two prodigious guitarists.

Ryan was twice a finalist in the BBC Young Folk Awards and twice a finalist in the BBC Radio Scotland Young Traditional Musician of the Year. Awarded Up and Coming Artist of the Year at the Scots Trad Music Awards in 2017, nominated for the Horizon Award at the BBC Radio 2 Folk Awards and named Musician of the Year in 2018 (Folking.com).

Title: A Hundred Words for Snow
Description: 'It's a bit weird to be sitting at the Arctic Circle chatting to a fit boy with your dad's ashes in your backpack.' Rory's dad was an explorer. Not literally, he was a geography teacher. But inside he was Bear Grylls. A teenage girl journeys to the North Pole with her father's ashes. A comic, complex, epic, undulating story that pitches themes of death and rebirth against a shifting backdrop of climate change, geography and exploration. A coming-of-age story with polar bears. Title: The Hippie Shakes
Description: Based on a true story, this new piece of gig theatre is a distinctly female story of motherhood, survival and intergenerational cycles of abuse. Chickie is a woman divided. She is torn between her desire for freedom and her responsibilities as a mother. She wants her husband's undivided love, but must grapple with him pulling the family into the illegal drug trade of the hippie movement. Set during the turbulent 60s and 70s, this one-woman show combines intimate storytelling, dark humour and live music to tell a truly incredible story.

Title: The Great American Songbook
Description: After an unbroken run from 1990 to 2019, Fife’s premier operatic concert group Ensemble is delighted to be able to return to the superb setting of St. Andrew’s and St. George’s West with a programme dipping into the Great American Songbook – the imaginary book that identifies the most important and influential popular songs from the 1920s right up to the 1970s and which live on from generation to generation. Most definitely an evening with something for everyone including hits such as Puttin’ on the Ritz, Embraceable You and Anything Goes.
Venue: St Andrew's and St George's West, George St
Venue description: A beautiful, easily accessible 18th century New Town church, which hosts a variety of musical performances – from soloists to choirs, instrumentalists to small orchestras and bands in all musical genres: classical, folk, jazz, songs from the shows, opera, world music.  Enjoy light lunches and snacks in the Undercroft cafe, or sit and admire the delightful Georgian interior.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, On street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The performance area and green room are not wheelchair accessible.  A ramp leads from the street up to the front portico for general access to the building. Lift access to cafe and toilets

Title: Paris: From Piaf to Pop!
Description: Christine Bovill’s award-winning Paris established her reputation as one of Europe’s finest interpreters of French song. In her new show, she travels into the 60s and the Americanisation of French music: le yé-yé. A time of great cultural change in France, would the high art of chanson survive...?  This new show offers a sexy and delicious celebration of the Golden Age of French song and how it evolved during the Swinging Sixties. Singing in both French and English she honours many stars including Edith Piaf, Jacques Brel, Serge Gainsbourg and Francoise Hardy.
Venue description: The Institut français d'Ecosse has been a historic Edinburgh Festival Fringe partner since opening in 1946. Our "Vive le Fringe !" programme highlights exceptional live performance from French and European artists and delivers events in conjunction with the International Festival, the Book Festival, and the Art Festival. Featuring fine dining and family-friendly shows, our stunning venue in the heart of the Old Town is an unmissable attraction for Fringe audiences.
Venue accessibility: Full venue site is accessible, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas. The Institut français d’Ecosse and the main performance space (Salle Emilienne Moreau-Evrard) are fully accessible with step-free access available. Because of current health guidelines, we operate with a one-way system throughout the building with entrance via George IV Bridge only and exit through West Parliament Square

Title: Chicago, Chicago!
Description: Set in – you guessed it – Chicago, a young woman named Lulu is looking for job after job. On her way to yet another job interview, she bumps into a group of women working at a strip bar. After chatting to them, thinking their lives sound like the dream, Lulu takes a job at the strip bar. With Lulu's fresh perspective, the women decide the way they are treated by the men around them is unacceptable. So, they take matters into their own hands by putting on the famed show – you probably guessed again – Chicago!
Venue description: Greenside @ Riddles Court marks a new chapter in Greenside’s journey. Over the years some familiar faces such as Dame Maggie Smith and Stephen Fry have graced the stages In this venue. With three spaces, a bar, beautiful courtyard seating Greenside @ Riddles Court is the perfect addition to our Green Family.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site, Wheelchair accessible toilet, No reserved accessible parking, No on street blue badge parking, Assistance dogs welcome in all areas

Title: Everything That's Me Is Falling Apart
Description: Using a mixture of animation, visualisation technology, a live camera and a toy train, comedian David Callaghan brings a groundbreaking comedy play packed with heartfelt, bittersweet and hilarious stories of love and loss. ‘The ripples of laughter constantly overlap, sometimes burbling along in appreciation between the punchlines’ **** (List). ‘One of my highlights of the fringe’ **** (Scotsman). 'Far more original than many big comedy names’ **** (EdfestMag.com). ‘He hits the mark, and scores’ **** (TheReviewsHub.com).
Venue description: Welcome to Infirmary Street! We can't wait to welcome you into our beautiful venue. We have four fantastic spaces this year showcasing the very best that the fringe has to offer. Hope to see you there!

Title: NEHH Presents... Christian Löffler
Description: Christian Löffler's art is heavily inspired by his environment. He lives and works, both as a painter and musician, in the remote Darss Peninsula in Germany's north-east and his atelier can be found within a rustic log cabin surrounded by overgrown wilderness overlooking the Baltic Sea. The area has provided him with the solitude necessary for his highly introspective work, while at the same time influencing him via its rugged landscapes in a continuous creative dialogue between artist and nature. This bucolic seclusion, tranquil by nature and intense in nature, has defined Löffler's body of work.
Venue description: Summerhall presents engaging, challenging and exhilarating theatre, music, dance and visual arts for people of all ages in the atmospheric buildings of Edinburgh’s former Royal (Dick) Veterinary College. There’s delicious food and drink in our own Royal Dick bar and Summerhall Café, plus al fresco bars and street food in the buzzing festival courtyard. The full programme of performance and exhibitions is at www.summerhall.co.uk
Venue accessibility:
We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. 

If coming into Summerhall using the main entrance please be aware that there are nine steps up to reception and the steps do not have a handrail.

Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café and our accessible venues. 

Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, there is parking using either pay and display machines or single yellow line spaces on Summerhall Square beside our step free access. Please be aware that this street is a dead end, and quite short and therefore parking there can be quite competitive.

We have lift access to some of the First Floor spaces and the Basement spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the Box Office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please contact us by phone on 0131 560 1581 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

Title: NEHH Presents... Rura
Description: Rura, an award-winning act are one of Scotland's most popular folk-based bands. The quartet's fiery, rugged and progressive instrumentals on fiddle, pipes, flute, guitar, keyboards and bodhran has placed them at the forefront of 21st century Scottish folk. Rura celebrated their tenth anniversary in 2020 with the release of their live album, Live at the Old Fruitmarket – recorded in front of a capacity crowd in February 2020 at Glasgow's Celtic Connections festival. This followed three acclaimed studio releases – most recently In Praise of Home, inspired by themes of belonging, heritage and a sense of place.

Title: NEHH Presents... Honeyblood
Description: Taking inspiration from dark and cloudy 90s indie rock luminaries like PJ Harvey, Sonic Youth, and Throwing Muses, Honeyblood is the project of Scottish singer/songwriter Stina Tweeddale. She gave her songs an indie pop crunch on early releases such as 2014's Honeyblood, then cranked up the amps on 2016's Babes Never Die, a loud and clear reflection of her alt-rock influences. She's joined live onstage by bandmates Debbie-Knox Hewson (Charli-XCX, James) and Anna Donigan (PINS) to create their most powerful live show to date.

Title: NEHH Presents... Auntie Flo (DJ)
Description: Brian d'Souza is an award-winning sound artist, DJ, producer and performer 'taking world music into the future' (Guardian). He is a Scottish Album of the Year Award winner and was recently awarded Scottish Electronic Musician of the Year. Alongside dreamy strings and soulful brass expect earthquakes, polar ice melting and the lonely call of earth-monitoring satellites. Description: A moving one-woman show about the trials and tribulations of living with chronic pain. Written, created and performed by Tali Foxworthy-Bowers, this piece shares her personal experience of chronic back pain through comedy, spoken word and movement. This piece aims to shed light on all ‘invisible’ illnesses and ailments, to educate those who have not experienced chronic suffering and connect with those who have, allowing an opportunity for recognition and relief through shared experiences. Tali tells her story (and crucially, the story of many other chronic pain sufferers) with warmth, honesty and vulnerability.

Venue accessibility:
We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. 

If coming into Summerhall using the main entrance please be aware that there are nine steps up to reception and the steps do not have a handrail.

Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café and our accessible venues. 

Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, there is parking using either pay and display machines or single yellow line spaces on Summerhall Square beside our step free access. Please be aware that this street is a dead end, and quite short and therefore parking there can be quite competitive.

We have lift access to some of the First Floor spaces and the Basement spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the Box Office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please contact us by phone on 0131 560 1581 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

Cottage has recently been performed at the Durham Drama Festival, where it was awarded Best Show, Best Writing, Best Lighting Design and Best Actor.

Description: There’s a world just like our own, but there isn’t a word for sand. There’s a world just like our own, but the keys on pianos are in random order so pianists really have to work for it. There’s a world just like our own, but Edith Piaf regretted five things. JLR returns with a new stand-up show about the worlds we don’t live in, which is secretly actually about the one we do. 'A one man finger-in-the-dyke against the blandification of comedy' (Guardian). **** (Times).

Title: The Wild Unfeeling World
Description: A tender, furious and fragile reimagining of Moby Dick from Fringe-First Award winning writer and storyteller Casey Jay Andrews. It’s 4.30am: Dylan is lying on the roof-top of a multi-storey car park in Hounslow. She watches as jumbo jets rumble into the crisp dawn. A surreal and lyrical suburban fable about recklessly seeking something that is out of your grasp. Winner: Best Theatre, Adelaide Fringe Weekly Awards. Recommended: The Guardian's Top Shows of the 2019 Edinburgh Festival Fringe. 'Funny, and sad, and deeply human' (Scotsman). 'A blissful mix of poetry and sophisticated storytelling' (OnceAWeekTheatre.com).
Artist: Casey Jay Andrews, Lion House Theatre
Venue description: Summerhall presents engaging, challenging and exhilarating theatre, music, dance and visual arts for people of all ages in the atmospheric buildings of Edinburgh’s former Royal (Dick) Veterinary College. There’s delicious food and drink in our own Royal Dick bar and Summerhall Café, plus al fresco bars and street food in the buzzing festival courtyard. The full programme of performance and exhibitions is at www.summerhall.co.uk
Venue accessibility:
We are committed to making your visit to Summerhall an enjoyable experience and we are working to make our venue as accessible as possible. The building is B-listed and is over one hundred years old and not all of our spaces are fully accessible. 

If coming into Summerhall using the main entrance please be aware that there are nine steps up to reception and the steps do not have a handrail.

Our step free access is through the side entrance on Summerhall Square. The Royal Dick Bar and Restaurant is situated to your right as you come in (with a ramp at the rear of the bar) and there is a ramp directly ahead of you that leads to the Reception, Box Office, Shop and Café and our accessible venues. 

Although there is no on-site parking at Summerhall, especially during the Fringe, there is parking using either pay and display machines or single yellow line spaces on Summerhall Square beside our step free access. Please be aware that this street is a dead end, and quite short and therefore parking there can be quite competitive.

We have lift access to some of the First Floor spaces and the Basement spaces. Further information about individual spaces and shows can be obtained from the Box Office. If you would like more information about the accessibility of particular shows, or if you wish to arrange a familiarisation tour of the venue prior to the festival, please contact us by phone on 0131 560 1581 or by email on info@summerhall.co.uk

Our staff are here to help and if there is anything you need assistance with please do not hesitate to ask.

Ghosts of the Near Future is a cowboy-noir fever dream about extinction. Colliding music, storytelling and live micro-cinema, it is a hallucinatory road-trip through a vanishing landscape, a haunting collage of miracles and misdirection. It takes us to the brink of disaster and asks whether we’re ready for what comes next. At high noon, emma + pj present a final encore for a world living one minute to midnight.

Description: I wouldn’t put it past Greg... Michael and Sally haven’t seen their unorthodox best friend since leaving school, both of them having been distracted by their complex lives. When, after five years, they both receive an out of the blue text, their intrigue in the outrageous rumours surrounding him makes his invitation for a drink irresistible. This twisting dark comedy, sometimes verging on the absurd, is the debut play of Duck in Arms Theatre Company.

Description: The Queens of Cups draw upon their years teaching, in OffFest nominee Bad Teacher. Evie, our titular teacher, takes you with her as she battles through the school day, confronting audiences with eye-opening truths about gender politics, mental health, and the outrageous expectations that our current educational system sets for students and teachers alike. 'The play is fast-paced and crude, but also allows us to see the person behind the job, and the vulnerability of the students. Both performance and direction are perfectly executed, and you couldn’t ask any more from a performer' ***** (NorthWestEnd.com).

Description: Alex MacKeith (2020 Musical Comedy Awards winner) delivers his debut show. Join Alex and his guitar and hopefully other audience members on an acoustic odyssey of songs that are playful, dark and maximum three minutes long*. If you’re looking for a sexy, confident musical comedian, by all means please find one and bring them to this. 'Hilarious' (Time Out). 'Ridiculously hilarious' (Skinny). Description: Harun Musho'd is an Arabic name. Good news is I can't drive. Bad news is I have a rucksack. If you don't like that joke, don't come to this show. 'Excellent Show. Sharp and witty comedy from a rising star.' (FringeReview.co.uk). 'A great comedian' **** (ViewsFromTheGods.co.uk). Title: head/lining
Description: A profound, thrilling mix of music and storytelling, head/lining is a lyrical deep dive inside the mind of a working-class white lad coming to terms with his life so far; from noxious upbringing to alcoholism and homelessness. Finding absolution in words and poetry, writer/performer Charlie Heptinstall’s spoken-word/indie-rock gig confronts an individual’s battle with identity and mental health, combined with Britain’s ever-growing prejudicial obsession with class. After a sell-out run at The Pleasance, OffComm award-winning head/lining (directed by Matt Strachan) has been described as punchy and fast-paced, offering audiences an insight into the harsh and angry struggles that go unspoken.
Warnings:
Use of strong language/swearing. References of drugs and alcohol. Physical reference of a suicide attempt. References of suicide. References of homelessness.

Description: Amputation is the only way!  Dick 'One Man in 100,000', a comic tragedy of hope over death, tells Richard Stamp's shock diagnosis of penis cancer. Smashing taboos of manhood, this is his cocktale. Unique and startlingly honest autobiographical travelogue: a life changing discovery, a medical journey with home truths. As seen on Channel 5's documentary Shopping for A New Penis, ITV's This Morning and Channel 4's Stand Up To Cancer. Written by James Chaplin. Original soundtrack by Ben Raine. Films and animation by Squire Studios. Supported by Orchid Male Cancer Charity (Helpline 08088020010). Produced by Certain Blacks.
Warnings: Nudity, Scenes of a sexual nature, Strong language/swearing

Title: Standing at the Back
Description: Self-doubt? Low self-esteem? Well, this sounds cheery. But what gives some of us the big swagger? And can the rest of us get it? After decades standing at the back, Mel Byron decided it was time to step forward and learn how to let her light shine. But where do you even find the light? Laugh along  as Mel fumbles her way to the front combining her own story with science, history and hair-dos to see if, in the words of George Eliot, ‘It is never too late to be what you might have been.'

Title: Phil Ellis: Hedgehog
Description: After the huge success of his last ever sell-out show, Edinburgh award-winning comedian Phil Ellis is back with his latest final stand-up show ever. Edinburgh panel prize winner, 2014. Star of BBC Radio 4's Phil Ellis is Trying. Seen on Comedy Central’s Roast Battle, The Russell Howard Hour, Channel 4, BBC Three, BBC Two and Dave. 'Nothing is ever what it seems in a Phil Ellis show... there are surprises and treats lurking in every nook and cranny' **** (List).
