In Dean’s The King is Dead, Prince James is suddenly thrust into the spotlight as he takes the throne following his father’s death. In Green’s high-school tale Gay Club!, Barney is desperate to become president of his school’s LGBTQIA+ society. Is fame worth it? Armed with only one photo of the two of them, Anthony created a loving, gentle and caring vision of his father, the proud new dad. And his father was all of those things. He was also a fully initiated member of a prominent Italian organised crime family. A compelling storyteller with a gag-rate to match, US comic Anthony DeVito (Comedy Central; HBO) makes his much-anticipated Edinburgh debut. Every single day, an all-star cast improvise a brand new Jane Austen novel based entirely on a single suggestion from the audience. Ask him anything you like! Created by record-breaking playwright Jonathan Maitland, inspired by his play The Last Temptation Of Boris Johnson. Our stories anthropomorphise the scientific world, giving atoms personalities to explain their behaviour, adding emotions to chemical reactions and inserting the idiosyncrasies of science into the day-to-day. We will reawaken the curiosity that your science teacher crushed.

Watch as Semi-Toned wow the audience with their trademark witty style, futuristic harmonies and energetic choreography whilst attempting to become the first a-cappella group to travel through time. Title: Esa Aldegheri: The Freedom Drive
Teaser: It’s the stuff of dreams. Esa Aldegheri sets out, carefree, from Orkney on a motorbike with her partner. In the cold fog of winter they cross to the citrus orchards of the Mediterranean, then on to the Syrian hills of Hatay, then Pakistan, India,...
Description: It’s the stuff of dreams. Esa Aldegheri sets out, carefree, from Orkney on a motorbike with her partner. In the cold fog of winter they cross to the citrus orchards of the Mediterranean, then on to the Syrian hills of Hatay, then Pakistan, India, China… For 18 months they travel, crossing 20 international borders, exploring the complexities of freedom, womanhood and human connection. Aldegheri discusses her transformative journey in Free to Go, in this horizon-expanding event with Nadine Aisha Jassat.

Title: Alright?
Description: 'Happy Birthday to me. 15. The end of the world!' Like a lot of 15-year-olds, Noah finds life difficult. Very difficult. And he doesn't know how to cope. This is a story about coping... about getting by. As Noah's dad says: 'You've gotta laugh!' But what if it's not funny… How do you cope when you're clearly not Alright? The original production, written by the award-winning Patrick Withey, is a brutally honest and quick-witted insight into living with mental health.
Venue description: Hugely popular Royal Mile venue located at the very heart of the festival. Part of our Royal Mile hub of 10 performance spaces. Title: The Gods, The Gods, The Gods
Description: Four stories; 14 tracks. A show full of big beats, soaring melodies and heart-stopping spoken word. Wright & Grainger, the creators of international smash-hit shows Orpheus and Eurydice, call us to the crossroads where mythology meets real life. The Gods are gathering, and you're invited. 'One of the great highlights of a decade of Fringe' ***** (SeeSawMag.com.au). 'This is immediate interactive theatre at its best' (StageWhispers.com.au). 'Captivating, electrifying and brings the house down' (CollageAdelaide.com). Previous awards: Best Theatre (Adelaide Fringe). Best in Fringe (Dunedin Fringe). Best Theatre Weekly (Fringe World). Best Music (Sydney Fringe).

Title: Imogen Binnie: The Great American Road Trip Reimagined
Teaser: The publication of Imogen Binnie’s first novel Nevada in 2013 was a watershed moment in transgender fiction. Following a trans punk woman, Nevada reflects on gender, heteronormativity and social conditioning as its protagonist flits across America in...
Description: The publication of Imogen Binnie’s first novel Nevada in 2013 was a watershed moment in transgender fiction. Following a trans punk woman, Nevada reflects on gender, heteronormativity and social conditioning as its protagonist flits across America in search of self-realisation. Binnie is joined by Harry Josephine Giles to celebrate the first UK publication of this seismic cult classic and discuss how – if at all – things have changed in the last nine years.

Title: Gabriel Krauze & Ryan O'Connor: Penned in the Margins
Teaser: Gabriel Krauze’s Who They Was is a visceral semi-autobiographical novel about a man living in the brutal gang world of south London while also studying for a degree. Ryan O’Connor’s The Voids, set in a condemned Glasgow high-rise full of...
Description: Gabriel Krauze’s Who They Was is a visceral semi-autobiographical novel about a man living in the brutal gang world of south London while also studying for a degree. Ryan O’Connor’s The Voids, set in a condemned Glasgow high-rise full of hedonistic benders and comic hallucinations, is a wild literary ride. Today, we welcome two fearless authors whose prose nods to the likes of Irvine Welsh and James Kelman. They speak to Graeme Armstrong.

Title: Matthieu Aikins, Sally Hayden & Polly Pallister-Wilkins: Bordering on Inhumane
Teaser: Deemed by Sally Rooney as the ‘most important work of contemporary reporting’, My Fourth Time, We Drowned explores Sally Hayden’s staggering investigation into the migrant crisis across North Africa. In The Naked Don’t Fear the Water, journalist...
Description: Deemed by Sally Rooney as the ‘most important work of contemporary reporting’, My Fourth Time, We Drowned explores Sally Hayden’s staggering investigation into the migrant crisis across North Africa. In The Naked Don’t Fear the Water, journalist Matthieu Aikins follows his friend Omar as he flees his war-torn country. And in Humanitarian Borders, Polly Pallister- Wilkins interrogates the humanitarian responses to border violence. A vital event for our times, chaired by Esa Aldegheri.

Title: Kehinde Andrews, Charlie Brinkhurst-Cuff & Marcus Ryder: A Celebration of Black Lives
Teaser: George Floyd’s murder by a white police officer in the US sparked Britain’s largest wave of protests against racism. Black British Lives Matter is a collection of essays gathered by equality advocate Marcus Ryder and his co-editor Lenny Henry. They...
Description: George Floyd’s murder by a white police officer in the US sparked Britain’s largest wave of protests against racism. Black British Lives Matter is a collection of essays gathered by equality advocate Marcus Ryder and his co-editor Lenny Henry. They honour Black excellence and explore the challenges Black people face in Britain, with contributors from Doreen Lawrence to David Olusoga. Black British Lives Matter is also a podcast produced by Ryder and Henry, which starts broadcasting this coming autumn. Join Marcus Ryder and contributor Charlie Brinkhurst-Cuff, who take to the stage alongside Jeffrey Boakye, who features in the podcast, to hear their response to a moment of outcry and optimism.

Title: Jessica Au & Stephanie Sy-Quia: Dreams of a Common Language
Teaser: Novelist Jessica Au and poet Stephanie Sy-Quia consider relationships across the generations and the possibilities of language in two spellbinding works of art. Winner of the 2020 Novel Prize, Au’s debut novella, Cold Enough for Snow, meditates on the...
Description:
Novelist Jessica Au and poet Stephanie Sy-Quia consider relationships across the generations and the possibilities of language in two spellbinding works of art. Winner of the 2020 Novel Prize, Au’s debut novella, Cold Enough for Snow, meditates on the nature of connection. Sy-Quia’s first collection of poems, Amnion, is an epic chronicle of family and migration. Join us for what is sure to be a riveting conversation with writer and activist Jessica Gaitán Johannesson.

	Jessica Au is appearing remotely.

Title: Imogen Binnie, Torrey Peters & Shola von Reinhold: A Golden Age for Trans Fiction

Description: In 2021, Torrey Peters became the first trans woman nominated for the Women’s Prize for Fiction – a milestone in the history of literature. Peters acknowledges that Detransition, Baby builds on the legacy of writers including Imogen Binnie – author of the ground-breaking novel Nevada. Today, Peters, Binnie and author of Lote, Shola von Reinhold, talk with Harry Josephine Giles about the evolution of trans literature.

Title: An Introduction to Writing Children's Books
Teaser: Let writer Simon James Green and agent Lindsey Fraser lead you on your journey to writing children’s books. Alongside Caroline Deacon and Onie Tibbitt from the Society of Children’s Book Writers and Illustrators, they help you understand how to...
Description: Let writer Simon James Green and agent Lindsey Fraser lead you on your journey to writing children’s books. Alongside Caroline Deacon and Onie Tibbitt from the Society of Children’s Book Writers and Illustrators, they help you understand how to narrow your idea down to a genre or reading level; whether your big idea is big enough for young adults or too big for a picture book. Come along to this practical workshop to find where your story fits. Suitable for writers at all stages – there’s no pressure to share your work.

Title: The Silver Bell
Description: A tale as old as time: boy meets boy, boy loses boy, boy punches hole in universe to get boy back. Join Alan Flanagan (Hollyoaks) and Brendan O'Rourke (Game Of Thrones) as they tell you their reality-bending story of love, loss and trying to find decent sausage rolls in a universe that never invented Greggs. 'A heart-warming tale with a clever twist… put The Silver Bell on your must-see list' **** (LondonLivingLarge.com). 'Heart-warming and moving' **** (BroadwayBaby.com).

She is unapologetically honest and impulsive in sharing her frustrations, erotic fantasies, connections and disconnections with men and nature. Her relatable vulnerabilities make Hard Shoulder a double-edged experience of quick-witted humour and heartache. Who can she verifiably trust? Her boyfriends? Her brother? The North Sea? Written and performed by Olivia Nicholson and produced by award-winning Sugar Butties, Hyenas! take the audience on a tequila-fuelled, anxiety inducing cocaine catfight. Everybody knows the bride is making the biggest mistake of her life but her "friends" are too sh*t-faced to care. Let's face it, they're only here for the likes on Instagram. Hyenas! focuses on themes of domestic abuse, loneliness and the pressures of social media on women today. ***** (MixUpTheatre.com). ***** (NorthWestEnd.co.uk).
Artist: Olivia Nicholson of Sugar Butties / Free Festival
Venue description: The Counting House has been a free venue for over a decade, and is one of the largest free venues in Edinburgh, with six rooms between this venue and it's linked venues 32 Below and The Pear Tree every day from 10:00 to 03:00. There's a massive outdoor courtyard, four bars, a full restaurant food selection and giant Outdoor screen. What better place could you hang out during the Fringe?

Title: Richard Todd: Transferable Skills
Description: With a busted knee, a burst eardrum and heroic reveries replaced by painkillers and words like 'ouch', 'pardon' and 'I'm down here!’, Todd reckons he has one last chance to reinvent himself, and just enough body parts to do it. A new show from award-winning stand-up Richard Todd. **** (Chortle.co.uk). **** (List). **** (Skinny). **** (Fest). 'Some comics have a gift of words that touches their work with wonder. Richard Todd is such a comic… Painfully funny… like finding The Fall guesting on X-Factor' **** (Scotsman).
Venue description: Opium alternative bar and nightclub is Edinburgh's longest running dedicated rock venue. Open seven days a week until 5am, Opium offers the very best in alternative entertainment. From rockaoke to live bands. During the Fringe we host a wide selection of top, five-star PBH Free Fringe comedy. Over 18s only.
Venue accessibility: Limited access to some parts of venue site. There are two steps into the bar area and downstairs room. There are then 10 steps to upstairs room

Title: .22 Comeback Special – Sir Dickie Benson
Description: The drunk knight returns. Haunted by Cher's ghost and pursued by Ridley Scott's Geordie goon squad, endling Hollywood hellraiser Sir Dickie Benson attempts to circumnavigate court-enforced sobriety, exercise (sic) his various demons and sabotage his own ill-advised/legally obligated comeback special: a masterclass presentation detailing the secrets to surviving the Hollywood system. Highly interactive, semi-improvised character comedy from an ADHD-addled mind.
Warnings:
Several light-hearted references to the occult, satanism, cannibalism, capitalism, addiction, alcoholism, drug abuse, sexuality, deviance, suicide and celebrity culture.
Audience participation, More information

Title: Dream of a King
Description: On April 3rd 1968, Martin famously gave a speech that was a premonition of his own death. The next day, on the balcony of the Lorraine Motel, he was shot and killed by an assassin’s bullet. Using creative licence and based on true events, Dream of a King is a reimagining of the hours leading up to the killing of Martin Luther King Jr and seeks to discover the man behind the icon. Christopher returns to theSpaceUK with his 2019 self-penned critically-acclaimed solo production. Not to be missed! 'An engaging performance' (Robert Beck, BroadwayBaby.com).
Artist: Christopher Tajah Resistance Theatre Company Ltd
Venue description: Next door to theSpace @ Surgeons Hall, theSpaceTriplex makes up part of our fabulously smart destination hub of 10 performance spaces located right at the heart of the modern Fringe and offers an unmissable platform of diverse live performance. Title: Shadow Under a Setting Sun
Description: When Coretta Scott King became widowed after an assassin's bullet murdered her husband, the iconic Martin Luther King Jr, it propelled her voice, activism and leadership onto the international stage. What was it like being the wife of such a famous leader? How did she cope with his loss whilst being thrust into the public spotlight? In the days following the killing, Coretta continued his work taking his place at planned marches and speaking engagements. This new solo woman play opens with Coretta giving a speech to university students. Written and directed by Christopher Tajah.

Title: Paul Savage: Well Groomed
Description: Paul Savage wanted to do a fun, silly show but shows about trauma win awards. So he's written a fun, silly show about his trauma. Trigger warning: Paedophile Jokes – but about them, not from the point of view of one, obviously. 'Genuinely brilliant, and all-round hoot' (Guardian). 'Paul Savage was a revelation' **** (ABC Australia). 'Armed with a razor-sharp wit, and serious pun-making abilities' (Advertiser, Adelaide). 'An engaging and affable labour of love from a man determined to find comedy in the unlikeliest of places' (BroadwayBaby.com). Top 10 Jokes of the Fringe, 2017 (Guardian).

Title: April in Ambleside
Description: Following a succesful Fringe run in 2019, Tony Randle is back with a blend of acoustic guitar pieces crossing genres from classical to jazz, via folk. This time reflecting on a chance meeting in the Lakes... a tale involving an inspired person in search of their muse, who also inspired him. Including many new compositions from lockdown, Tony, as ever, continues to popularise the use of the classical guitar in genres it was never designed for, whilst stopping by some classics.
Venue: St Andrew's and St George's West, George St
Venue description: A beautiful, easily accessible 18th century New Town church, which hosts a variety of musical performances – from soloists to choirs, instrumentalists to small orchestras and bands in all musical genres: classical, folk, jazz, songs from the shows, opera, world music. Title: Wreckage
Description: Gangs of London star Andrew Laithwaite returns to the Fringe for the first time in a decade for his singer-songwriter debut as Laith Andrews, in an intimate journey of love and loss, sensitively told on the electric ukulele. What treasures hide in the wrecks of our relationships? Composed after two and a half years on the road, Wreckage is a vulnerable meditation on heartbreak and healing, that holds us by the hand through abandonment to rejuvenation. Praise for Gangs of London: **** (Guardian). **** (Empire). **** (Vulture.com).

Title: Alfa Fail
Description: Have you ever wondered: what makes a real man? What should he drink? What should he wear? And what on earth does he do when he’s out with the lads? Well professional over-thinker and stand up Jacob Moreton has done exactly that. Through a series of boisterous stories and laddish characters, audiences will explore what it means to be masculine in this gender-bending climate we find ourselves living in. Prepare yourself to experience the intense challenges that come with being so manly... like trying to light a fire without chipping a freshly painted nail.

Title: Symphonic Ibiza
Description: Featuring some of the most famous Ibiza club anthems from the last 30 years, celebrate the European island of clubbing this summer. Symphonic Ibiza fuses a thrilling live orchestra with high-tempo beats from renowned club DJ Andy Joyce and musical genius Steve Etherington, whose credentials include residencies at Ibiza super-clubs Pacha, Amnesia, Eden and Café Mambo. This party is like no other, creating an entirely new live experience. At Edinburgh's iconic McEwan Hall, this unforgettable night of heart-pounding dance classics is an epic way to round off your festival night out.

Title: Dykegeist
Description: Dykegeist, a choreographic performance from Manchester-born London-based artist Eve Stainton, with live sound performed by musician Mica Levi. Dykegeist is interested in complicating the archetypal narratives assigned to the lesbian predator. During the evening, aesthetics will shift between a supernatural thriller, a sci-fi spider lair, a haunted club scene, a social situation to discuss threat/consent/otherness. Audience may be invited to participate; extra care will be given to make it comfortable to decline. This performance has brought Stainton back to the Speed Garage sounds of Manchester's club scene, originating in African American soul and exploding in Northern England.
Artist: Eve Stainton with Mica Levi / Horizon showcase

Description: The Welsh optimist returns to the festival, and this year he's been thinking about the future. The result? 45 minutes of excellent stand-up comedy. This is Steffan's fifth solo show for Edinburgh. Includes support acts hand-picked by Steffan himself. Warm, friendly stand-up comedy from Wales – just the thing for a post-pandemic festival.

Title: The Evolution of Young Adult Literature
Teaser: What are the limits and boundaries of writing difficult themes in books for young adults? Join award-winning young adult authors Juno Dawson and Faridah Àbíké-Íyímídé alongside literary agent Davinia Andrew-Lynch and social media consultant Jean...
Description: What are the limits and boundaries of writing difficult themes in books for young adults? Join award-winning young adult authors Juno Dawson and Faridah Àbíké-Íyímídé alongside literary agent Davinia Andrew-Lynch and social media consultant Jean Menzies as they delve into this important genre. Chaired by Caroline Carpenter, from the YA Book Prize, our panellists explore the novels that have tackled complex subject matter and discuss how writing for young adults has evolved.

Title: Call My Agent! The Role of the Literary Agent
Teaser: What does a literary agent’s day look like? Discover the intricacies of the role with Heather Parry, co-founder of Extra Teeth literary magazine and the Society of Authors’ Senior Policy and Liaison Manager for Scotland. Joined by an impressive...
Description: What does a literary agent’s day look like? Discover the intricacies of the role with Heather Parry, co-founder of Extra Teeth literary magazine and the Society of Authors’ Senior Policy and Liaison Manager for Scotland. Joined by an impressive line-up of literary agents, Parry chairs a discussion that explores current trends in the book industry, what agents look for in submissions and how they work with writers. Featuring Abi Fellows (The Good Literary Agency), Chloe Seager (Madeleine Milburn Literary, TV & Film Agency), Emma Paterson (Aitken Alexander Associates) and Isobel Dixon (Blake Friedmann Literary Agency).

Title: Clementine
Description: Meet Lady Clementine. From shipwrecks to guillotines, bad luck has plagued her love life from day one. When her latest beau, Sir Bradley, goes missing, she sets off on a quest to solve the mystery of her ill-fortune. Guided by the stars, she soon finds out she's been searching for love in all the wrong places. Set roughly "in the past", expect dashing dandies, sickly sisters and many, many, many letters. Not for men. (Unless you're a single Leo in possession of a good fortune). Vault Festival-selected show.
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Caves

Title: The Masks of Oscar Wilde
Description: Man of letters. Aesthete. Victorian moralist. Playwright. Oscar Wilde wore many masks. But as a well–meaning professor and his eager student trace the life of the legendary writer, it becomes clear there may be more masks waiting in the shadows. As they dig deeper, we begin to wonder. Are they hiding something? What if some masks are better left in the shadows? A test of wits, of "truth", and an examination of the fabulous and scandal-ridden life of Oscar Wilde and the man behind the masks.
Venue description: Greenside @ Riddles Court marks a new chapter in Greenside’s journey. Title: Vix Leyton: Pedestrian
Description: A whirlwind show examining the multiple roles you play in your life and what happens when you break out of them. Everyone has that friend who tweeted something that altered the course of their life. If you don't, Vix is now yours. Part cautionary tale on keeping hold of yourself and not believing your own hype, part inspiration for anyone who might want to give a dream a go. It really could happen to you and there is power in saying yes to the things that scare you.
Venue: Just the Tonic at The Mash House

After a sell-out run at the Edinburgh Horror Festival 2021, the Crested Fools are delighted to bring this gothic masterpiece to Paradise in the Vault – a unique fusion of theatre, storytelling and choreography perfect for an eerie evening at the Fringe. ‘A polished, creepy storytelling experience… an often unnerving and always interesting performance [with] a tangible sense of stylised dread’ **** (TheWeeReview.com).

This guided session will offer both learners and fluent speakers the chance to understand the contribution of Gaelic speakers to the history of the armed forces.

Description: Cambridge Footlights Robbie, Emily and Maddie have been living together in harmony… well, almost. Robbie hogs the bathroom, Emily never washes up, Maddie’s food’s grown sentient life and did anyone notice that fourth housemate? Join the trio as they air their own dirty laundry and some others’ along the way. From the vigilante neighbourhood watch WATCH committee to a milkman with a dark and mysterious past, everything comes out in the wash. This show puts an absurdist spin on day-to-day domestics: an assortment of shorts, characters, and songs, it’s a mixed load and a guaranteed bundle of laughs!

Venue description:
The Main Hall is one of the most prestigious venues in the City of Edinburgh, an iconic landmark which sits atop Mound Place, near Edinburgh Castle. Owned by the Church of Scotland, from 1999-2004 it was used as the home of the new Scottish Parliament. 

The Assembly Hall was designed by David Bryce in 1858. One of the most significant historical events took place in 1910 when 1355 delegates were in Edinburgh for the World Missionary Conference on 14 June, the beginnings of the 'ecumenical movement'. The Assembly Hall boasts a striking multi-tiered and galleried interior and a black and white marble corridor.

The first successful artistic production hosted by the hall took place in 1948, when an adaptation of Sir David Lyndsay's The Thrie Estaites, the first performance of this play since 1552, was staged to great acclaim. 

Until 1999, the Assembly Hall was rarely used except for meetings of the General Assembly. The hall continues today, each summer, to be used as a venue for the Edinburgh Jazz and Blues Festival and Edinburgh Festival Fringe.

Scottish blues-rock singer Maggie Bell first gained prominence fronting 70s Scots rock heroes, Stone the Crows, and her raunchy, high energy style has electrified audiences all over the world in a career of 50 years. Amazingly, she’s still touring; constantly preaching the blues, with all of her powers intact, often, as tonight, in the company of a band featuring guitarist, Sandy Tweeddale.

Description:
We are opening the 2022 Festival in style, celebrating the First Lady of Song, Ella Fitzgerald. 

Arguably one of the finest female jazz vocalists of all time, her extraordinary diction, timing, sense of swing and all-round joie de vie made her one of the finest interpreters of the great American song book. 

Violinist, vocalist and broadcaster Seonaid Aitken is the ideal choice to celebrate Ella and the songs she made famous, including ‘A Tisket A Tasket’, ‘Lady be Good’ ‘How High The Moon’, ‘Ev’ry Time We Say Goodbye’, ‘Summertime’, and ‘The Very Thought of You’. Fronting a superstar big band with special guests including Glaswegian rising star singer kitti, saxophonist Konrad Wiszniewski and Italian trumpeter Daniele Raimondi, this will be an evening of inspiring music, celebrating a jazz legend.

The Main Hall is one of the most prestigious venues in the City of Edinburgh, an iconic landmark which sits atop Mound Place, near Edinburgh Castle. Owned by the Church of Scotland, from 1999-2004 it was used as the home of the new Scottish Parliament. 

The Assembly Hall was designed by David Bryce in 1858. One of the most significant historical events took place in 1910 when 1355 delegates were in Edinburgh for the World Missionary Conference on 14 June, the beginnings of the 'ecumenical movement'. The Assembly Hall boasts a striking multi-tiered and galleried interior and a black and white marble corridor.

The first successful artistic production hosted by the hall took place in 1948, when an adaptation of Sir David Lyndsay's The Thrie Estaites, the first performance of this play since 1552, was staged to great acclaim. 

Until 1999, the Assembly Hall was rarely used except for meetings of the General Assembly. The hall continues today, each summer, to be used as a venue for the Edinburgh Jazz and Blues Festival and Edinburgh Festival Fringe.

Fronted by fiddle player and sophisticated songstress, Seonaid Aitken, Rose Room combine brilliant musicianship and warm personality, recreating the excitement of Rive Gauche Paris of the 30s and 40s with Stephane Grappelli and Django Reinhardt. “Stupendous gypsy jazz, and a superb singer” (Scotsman).

Description: Newtongrange Silver Band is a traditional mining village brass band from the outskirts of Edinburgh, but their repertoire is far from traditional. In 2019, before the pandemic, the band had an extremely successful year winning a number of trophies at several brass band competitions, including the Scottish Brass Band Association Championship Section Band of the Year Award. Newtongrange Silver Band is delighted to return to the Fringe at Venue 405 after giving a sell-out, show-stopping concert in the 2019 programme. There’s something for everyone in this varied programme which also showcases its world class soloists.

Title: Sticky Door
Description: The 2014 plan was a simple one, I would Casanova myself around our nation's capital looking for consenting heterosexual adult males. One no-frills lover-man for every month. I was the original calendar girl. Helen Mirren plays me in the film. A storytelling show with songs about sex, stigma and cystitis, by someone who has experienced all three. From the multi award-winning team that bought you the 'exquisite' (List) Sexy Lamp, and Bicycles and Fish. 'Arnstein is an incredible performer who seems primed for greatness' (Guardian). 'Plays as good as this are rare' ***** (TheReviewsHub.com).

Title: Room – A Room of One's Own
Description: It is 1929. Woolf is ordered off the path and refused entry to the library. Why? Woolf demands answers. Woolf unflinchingly interrogates the crushing injustice she encounters. Woolf slices through notions of gender disparity with visceral integrity and ironic charm. An innovative dramatic interpretation of an iconic text. 'The outstanding one-person show I've seen this Fringe … an exquisite performance. Alexander's fine performance is searing and visceral' ***** (FringeReview.co.uk). 'Pitch Perfect' ***** (TheReviewsHub.com). 'Alexander lit up the stage as she portrayed one of the most fearless female writers in history' **** (BroadwayBaby.com).

Description: During a bizarre childhood accident, Trevor was drenched head to toe in dragon's blood. Growing green and scaly skin, he withdrew from the world. Tonight – 20 years later – Trevor meets a cute guy on a first date and ends up on an adventure of mythic proportions. Equal parts comic book lore and coming-of-age love story, Lizard Boy is the thrilling original rock musical that's been called 'ingenious' (San Francisco Chronicle), 'phenomenal' (MercuryNews.com) and 'ferocious and funny' (Seattle Times). Featuring the award-winning, original American cast and starring author/actor Justin Huertas.

Description: A woman grieving for the loss of her daughter is drawn to the mystery of the Wishing Well. She asks for her daughter back but this comes at a price. Will she be willing to accept the forfeit? This play premiered at the StagEHd festival to excellent reviews. A powerful drama with outstanding performances from all the cast. You can not fail to be moved by the plight of the grieving mother and the touches of comedy balance the intensity. The movement section of the play is choreographed by John Ross.

Description: Are you struggling to cope with the Fringe? Overwhelmed by producing a show? If you have any anxiety or concern then these sessions are for you, along with anyone looking for help or an understanding of mental health. These are specially tailored mental health training sessions for performers, delivered by the multi-award winning National charity Chasing The Stigma. This short informative free session helps provide understanding of mental health, mental illness and what to do if you or somebody else needs help and support.

Mr.B has spent the last fifteen years touring the world, releasing eleven albums of whimsical, dandy hip-hop, streaming cocktail parties and generally being a well-dressed sillybugger. Description: Escape from the House of Mercy is a dance/theatre work which looks at institutions which have compromised the rights of women in the past and the present through the buried stories and embodied history of the workhouses of the US and Ireland. The performance includes movement, voice and visual elements to create a world which considers the distance travelled and the road still ahead for women’s rights around the world.

This dynamic two-hander joins two sisters rekindling their relationship over a handful anger management sessions and plenty of gin drinking. Jude wonders if having children is the only way to lead a fulfilling life. The pressure of making the "right" choice is amplified when it seems that neither time nor her sister is on her side. Teaser: Led by the Italian pianist Sade Mangiaracina, this trio plays beautiful, beguiling music, blending classical music with European jazz and Mediterranean influences.
Description:
Led by the Italian pianist Sade Mangiaracina, this trio plays beautiful, beguiling music, blending classical music with European jazz and Mediterranean influences. Her music tonight has been inspired by the symbol of the struggle for human rights: Nelson Mandela. Mangiaracina is a major new discovery for subtlety, finesse and great touch and for a set of compelling compositions that draw audiences into the mesmeric atmospheres she creates.

The largest is Roxy Central, where our streaming programme takes place. This is a truly unique and beautiful space, with original features, a large stage and a bar area.

Description: Why toddle when you can dance? Join DJ Monski Mouse and her dancers for an epic session of bonkers, bopping, beautiful fun. Expect high-energy smiling to retro beats and thumping nursery rhymes. Get your disco-dancing booties on! 'Tune after tune perfectly chosen for the youngsters' ***** (Edinburgh Evening News). Warnings:

Description: This feel-good show connects audiences with the energy, excitement and raw emotion of the pioneering R&B and soul acts of the 1940s, 1950s and 1960s. Crafted by eight-piece R&B band Ken Wood and the Mixers, the show uses words, music and a dynamic stage show to tell the story of soul. Anecdotes, humour and the songs of Otis Redding, Sam and Dave, James Brown, Smokey Robinson and many more are all brought together through performances crackling with energy. Her home is full of hand-painted cupboards full of vintage, her small but gorgeous garden bursts forth in a chaos of colour each spring and summer, bright clothes swinging from the washing line above. The Song School walls are covered with murals by Phoebe Traquair, painted between 1888 and 1892. The murals include religious images, images of the natural world, and portraits of leading figures of the day and of the choir and clergy of the time.

Description: Red rubber strands hang down, filling the space. Three girls, traces of this world, wander through the red forest, tracing fragmented memories of their lives before the blast. What was this blast? What happened? They trace their journey through improvised choreography, music and words. This work explores unreal childhood nightmares as a metaphor for the lost feeling of home, the altered memory of a pet cat and the messages that one would deliver at their last. Three separate, yet unified pieces, that together interweave the experience of life resonating in a turbulent world.

Title: Modular Music and Pattern Language Workshop
Description: The four-hour modular music creation workshop, designed and led by Raphael Mak based in Stockholm, Sweden, leads participants through a unique creative process by exploring and creating music spatially with Lego blocks. Participants work in groups of 3-5 people and are guided by a pattern language, which includes different methods and elements in how to plan and write the music. Participants are invited to bring their own instruments, if they have them, to play their creation at the end of the workshop.

Title: Shattered
Description: In third grade, Diana kicked her crush in the crotch and her love life didn’t improve from there. What starts as an innocent look into her relationship past, turns into a comedic and heartbreakingly raw exploration of dating, dysfunction and sexual devastation told through the voices of 35 characters. Using comedy to take us through tragedy, Shattered ultimately tells of one individual picking up the broken pieces of herself and learning to live again. ‘A woman of 1,000 faces’ (SplashMags.com). ‘Truly epic’ (NoHoArtsDistrict.com). ‘A real tour-de-force’ **** (BouquetsBrickbatsReviews.com). ‘A raw, visceral dissection of the human psyche’ ***** (BroadwayBaby.com).
